newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel offers soften on crude fall.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel offers soften on crude fall.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was quiet on Thursday but offers fell a little on the back of a plunge in crude oil futures, traders said.
Two refiners offering early in the day at $103/$104 for 0.5 to 0.7 pct sulphur material moved down a little after crude came off.
One said he may hold making a deal until Friday to see if crude futures would reverse their downward trend.

"If it holds at $17.90 then we may do something at that level and if it falls further then we'll be below $103," a refinery trader said, adding that a second refiner will come down from his offer at $103.

"Generally offers were on the higher side earlier in the day with lack of supplies and good buying interest but then crude came down. But if crude picks back up overnight, it (low sulphur straight-run) will go back up," the trader added.
A third seller was sticking to $105 fob for better quality material.
High sulphur straight-run continued to be offered on the high side for E-4 which was reported very scarce.
M-100 continued to be offered at a premium of two means plus $4/$5, steady to a bit weaker than a day earlier. But traders said buying interest was still coming into the market.
